Package com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp

Class SmiFormatter

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.SmiFormatter
public final class SmiFormatter extends Object
Renders SNMP/SMI values as human-readable display strings — the kind of formatting a MIB browser applies when it shows the result of a GET. Everything here is pure, static and side-effect free, and the API is deliberately dependency-free: it takes JDK primitives, byte[] and BigInteger rather than any SNMP-library value type, so it can format bytes decoded from any source (or from tests) without pulling in SNMP4J.

The SMI base types are unsigned even though Java has no unsigned primitives, so the numeric helpers here interpret their input accordingly:

  • formatCounter(long) and formatGauge(long) treat the argument as an unsigned 32-bit quantity (Counter32 / Gauge32 / Unsigned32), masking to 32 bits so that both 4294967295L and its signed twin -1L render as 4294967295.
  • formatCounter64(BigInteger) and formatCounter64(long, long) render an unsigned 64-bit Counter64.

  • Method Details

    • formatTimeTicks

      public static String formatTimeTicks(long hundredths)
      Formats a TimeTicks value — hundredths of a second since some epoch — as "D days, H:MM:SS.ss", e.g. 12345 renders as "0 days, 0:02:03.45" and 8640000 (one day) as "1 days, 0:00:00.00". Hours are not zero-padded; minutes, seconds and hundredths always have two digits.
      Parameters:
      hundredths - elapsed time in 1/100 s; must be non-negative
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if hundredths is negative

    • formatTimeTicksWithRaw

      public static String formatTimeTicksWithRaw(long hundredths)
      Like formatTimeTicks(long) but also appends the raw tick count in parentheses, e.g. "0 days, 0:02:03.45 (12345)" — the form typically shown alongside sysUpTime.

    • formatCounter

      public static String formatCounter(long value)
      Renders a Counter32 (a monotonically increasing unsigned 32-bit wrap-around counter). The argument is treated as unsigned 32-bit: only the low 32 bits are used, so -1L and 0xFFFFFFFFL both yield "4294967295".

    • formatGauge

      public static String formatGauge(long value)
      Renders a Gauge32 / Unsigned32 value. As with formatCounter(long), the argument is interpreted as unsigned 32-bit.

    • formatCounter64

      public static String formatCounter64(BigInteger value)
      Renders a Counter64 given as a non-negative BigInteger. The value is expected to fit in 64 unsigned bits; it is rendered in plain decimal.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if value is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if value is negative

    • formatCounter64

      public static String formatCounter64(long high, long low)
      Renders a Counter64 supplied as two 32-bit halves — high the most-significant word and low the least-significant — each interpreted as unsigned 32-bit. This is convenient when a 64-bit value has been split to avoid Java's signed long.

    • formatIpAddress

      public static String formatIpAddress(byte[] addr)
      Formats a 4-byte IpAddress as a dotted quad "a.b.c.d", each octet read unsigned so that a byte of (byte) 0xC0 becomes 192.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if addr is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if addr is not exactly four bytes long

    • formatOctetString

      public static String formatOctetString(byte[] bytes)
      Formats an OctetString: if every byte is printable ASCII it is returned as text, otherwise it is rendered as a space-separated hex dump (see hex(byte[])). An empty array yields an empty string. Use looksPrintable(byte[]), hex(byte[]) directly to force one form.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if bytes is null

    • looksPrintable

      public static boolean looksPrintable(byte[] bytes)
      True when every byte is printable 7-bit ASCII (in [0x20, 0x7E]). An empty array is considered printable (it renders as the empty string). Control bytes, 0x7F and any byte with the high bit set make this return false.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if bytes is null

    • hex

      public static String hex(byte[] bytes)
      Renders bytes as an upper-case, space-separated hex dump, e.g. {0xAA, 0xBB, 0xCC} becomes "AA BB CC". An empty array yields an empty string.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if bytes is null

    • formatObjectId

      public static String formatObjectId(long[] subIds)
      Formats an OBJECT IDENTIFIER given as its sub-identifiers into dotted form, e.g. {1,3,6,1,2,1,1,1,0} becomes "1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0". Reuses Oid for the arithmetic-safe rendering (each sub-identifier must be in [0, 2^32-1]).
      Throws:
      OidFormatException - if subIds is null/empty or any value is out of range

    • formatOid

      public static String formatOid(String oid)
      Normalises a dotted OID string, e.g. ".1.3.6.1" becomes "1.3.6.1". Passes through Oid.parse(String) so malformed input is rejected the same way.
      Throws:
      OidFormatException - if oid is not a valid dotted OID
